How many booked nights a short stay needs to beat a normal rental

Source: R/breakeven_nights.R
breakeven_nights.Rd

Compares the money from renting a whole home as a short stay with the money from a normal long-term lease. It answers one plain question: how many nights a month would the place need to be booked before it earns more than the rent?

Usage

breakeven_nights(
  place,
  bedrooms,
  weekly_rent = NULL,
  costs = 0.2,
  review_rate = 0.5,
  avg_stay = 3,
  listings = staysvic::vic_listings,
  reviews = staysvic::vic_reviews_monthly,
  rents = staysvic::vic_rents
)

Arguments

place

A single place name.

bedrooms

Number of bedrooms, 1 to 4. Four means four or more.

weekly_rent

Weekly rent you could get on a normal lease, in dollars. If NULL (the default), the latest Homes Victoria median for the place's suburb group is used, when one exists. Homes Victoria does not publish a median for every area (small towns such as Lorne and Port Campbell have none), so supply your own figure for those places.

costs

Share of each night's price lost to platform fees, cleaning, supplies and management. Defaults to 0.2 (20 per cent).

review_rate

Share of stays that end with a review. Defaults to 0.5.

avg_stay

Typical stay length in nights. Defaults to 3.

listings, reviews, rents

Data to use. Default to vic_listings, vic_reviews_monthly and vic_rents.

Value

A one-row tibble with place, bedrooms, n_listings, median_price, weekly_rent, rent_source, nights_needed, est_nights_avg, est_nights_peak, est_nights_low, peak_month, low_month, reliable (FALSE when the answer rests on too little data), note, a plain-language message that explains any problem, and monthly, a list column holding a tibble of estimated booked nights for each calendar month over the last 12 months.

Details

The calculation is

$$nights = \frac{weekly\ rent \times 52 / 12}{nightly\ price \times (1 - costs)}$$

where the nightly price is the median for active, whole-home short stays with the chosen number of bedrooms in that place.

To give the answer some context, it also estimates how many nights a typical listing in the place is actually booked each month. This uses the same rough rule as Inside Airbnb: about half of guests leave a review, and a typical stay is about three nights, so each review stands for roughly six booked nights. The estimate is capped at 21 nights a month (70 per cent of a month) so one very busy listing cannot push it to absurd levels. Treat it as a guide to the size of the gap, not a forecast.

Examples

breakeven_nights("Geelong", bedrooms = 3)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 15
#>   place   bedrooms n_listings median_price weekly_rent rent_source nights_needed
#>   <chr>      <int>      <int>        <dbl>       <dbl> <chr>               <dbl>
#> 1 Geelong        3         70         329.         480 Homes Vict…          7.90
#> # ℹ 8 more variables: est_nights_avg <dbl>, est_nights_peak <dbl>,
#> #   est_nights_low <dbl>, peak_month <chr>, low_month <chr>, reliable <lgl>,
#> #   note <chr>, monthly <list>

# Places with no published rent need your own figure
breakeven_nights("Port Campbell", bedrooms = 2, weekly_rent = 550)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 15
#>   place   bedrooms n_listings median_price weekly_rent rent_source nights_needed
#>   <chr>      <int>      <int>        <dbl>       <dbl> <chr>               <dbl>
#> 1 Port C…        2         27          400         550 Your figure          7.45
#> # ℹ 8 more variables: est_nights_avg <dbl>, est_nights_peak <dbl>,
#> #   est_nights_low <dbl>, peak_month <chr>, low_month <chr>, reliable <lgl>,
#> #   note <chr>, monthly <list>

# Use your own rent estimate and higher costs
breakeven_nights("Melbourne CBD", bedrooms = 1, weekly_rent = 550, costs = 0.3)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 15
#>   place   bedrooms n_listings median_price weekly_rent rent_source nights_needed
#>   <chr>      <int>      <int>        <dbl>       <dbl> <chr>               <dbl>
#> 1 Melbou…        1       1264         232.         550 Your figure          14.7
#> # ℹ 8 more variables: est_nights_avg <dbl>, est_nights_peak <dbl>,
#> #   est_nights_low <dbl>, peak_month <chr>, low_month <chr>, reliable <lgl>,
#> #   note <chr>, monthly <list>
